# Results

## Executable visualisation

The following Python cell evaluates @eq-response and creates @fig-damped-response. Its code is not displayed because `echo: false` is the project default; only the generated figure appears in the report.

```{python}
#| label: fig-damped-response
#| fig-cap: "Damped displacement response and exponential amplitude envelope."
#| fig-alt: "A decaying oscillatory displacement curve bounded by a dashed exponential envelope."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.2
import sys
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "code/python")
from brand import brand  # colours from org.primary-color / org.accent-color

m, c, k, x0 = 1.0, 0.8, 20.0, 0.10
omega_n = np.sqrt(k / m)
zeta = c / (2 * np.sqrt(k * m))
omega_d = omega_n * np.sqrt(1 - zeta**2)

t = np.linspace(0, 8, 800)
envelope = x0 * np.exp(-zeta * omega_n * t)
x = envelope * (
    np.cos(omega_d * t)
    + (zeta * omega_n / omega_d) * np.sin(omega_d * t)
)

b = brand()
navy, orange, muted = b["primary"], b["accent"], b["muted"]
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "font.sans-serif": ["Montserrat", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial"],
    "axes.labelcolor": b["ink"],
    "text.color": b["ink"],
    "xtick.color": muted,
    "ytick.color": muted,
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2), constrained_layout=True)
ax.plot(t, x, color=navy, linewidth=2.4, label="Displacement")
ax.plot(t, envelope, color=orange, linewidth=1.4, linestyle="--", label="Envelope")
ax.plot(t, -envelope, color=orange, linewidth=1.4, linestyle="--")
ax.axhline(0, color=b["line"], linewidth=1)
ax.set(xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="Displacement (m)")
ax.grid(axis="x", color=b["line"], linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.65)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.spines[["left", "bottom"]].set_color("#d9e2e8")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
plt.show()
```

The response remains within the analytical envelope and decays toward equilibrium. The first few extrema retain the oscillatory character of the underdamped model, while their magnitude decreases exponentially.

::: {.callout-warning title="Interpretation boundary"}
This example uses deterministic parameters and contains no measurement uncertainty. A real report should state uncertainty sources, validation data, and sensitivity assumptions before drawing engineering conclusions.
:::

## Summary indicators

The damping ratio is below one, so the chosen system is underdamped. The corresponding natural and damped frequencies are close because the damping is modest. These values are computed from @eq-parameters rather than entered manually, reducing the risk of inconsistency between the text, table, and plot.
